newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MARCH 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MARCH 13.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - After a 14 hour meeting yesterday, the cabinet reached a decision that, from July 1 of this year, rents will be able to increase in Prague by 100 percent, in other large cities by 62 percent, in cities with up to 100,000 residents by 50 percent and in smaller cities by 30 percent at the most. The cabinet also decided that from the middle of the year, the state will begin giving social support for the increase in rents. Expectations are that 160,000 families will receive aid this year of more than 200 million crowns.

- The cabinet approved the proposal from Education Minister Ivan Pilip which will increase the number of hours teachers are required to work by about two hours. This will increase teachers' wages by 500 to 1,000 crowns.

- Banka Hana signed a contract yesterday which will allow it to sell part of its bad credits amounting to about 1.9 billion crowns to Czech financial companies. It is the first bank to enter into this stabilisation programme which was approved by the cabinet last year.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Value added tax for electricity, gas and solid fuels should increase from the current five percent to 22 percent from January 1, 1998.
- The management of Czech Railways is convinced that it will succeed in closing a collective contract with the railway workers union for 1997 by the end of March.

- By the end of March, the Health Ministry wants to issue guarantees to 12 drug distributors that they will receive the money owed to them by hospitals. The ministry assures that the distributors will not stop supplying medicines to hospitals from April 1, as they are currently threatening.

PRAVO - The cabinet unexpectedly decided yesterday that the new director of the secret service (BIS) will be Karel Vulterin, the director of the central radioisotope laboratory of the First Faculty of Medicine at Charles University and the chairman of the university workers union.
- Industrial output decreased in fixed prices this January by 3.9 percent compared to January of 1996, according to the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU).
- Construction output decreased this January by 18.6 percent in comparison with January 1996, according to the CSU.

- Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka made a public offer for shares of Finop Holding. It is offering to buy individual shares nominally at 130 crowns, although they were trading on the stock market at 135 on Monday.
LIDOVE NOVINY - The National Property Fund will begin offering its 8.7 percent stake in Skoda Plzen either on the stock market or in the form of a public tender within a few weeks.
